title: Practical: Time Utilities Module
story: Time calculations appear everywhere: countdown timers, age calculators, scheduling systems. Build a time utilities module with days-in-month, leap-year checks, and duration formatting — the foundation for any time-aware program.
why: Time utility functions are surprisingly tricky (leap years, varying month lengths) and benefit from being centralized in a tested module.
analogy: A calendar on your wall already solved all the tricky date logic — you just flip to a month and trust it's right. A time utilities module is your programmatic calendar: it encodes the same rules once, correctly, so you never re-derive them.
try_it: Add `day_of_week(day, month, year)` using Zeller's formula. Add `days_between` that calculates the number of days between two dates. Write tests for edge cases: Feb 29 in non-leap years, month 13, day 0.
tips: Leap year rule is: divisible by 400 OR (divisible by 4 AND NOT divisible by 100)
30 days hath September, April, June, and November — all the rest have 31, except February
Use `is_valid_date` before any date operation to catch bad inputs early
common_mistakes: Getting the leap year rule wrong — 1900 was NOT a leap year, 2000 WAS
Not validating month/day ranges before accessing arrays or doing calculations
